label: prop:constant_subdifferential
title: Proposition
head: environment
name: constant subdifferential

title: Proof
body_md:
Consider the polyhedral set $\operatorname{epi}(f)$. The interior of each face of $\operatorname{epi}(f)$ is characterized by its normal cone. Furthermore, the normal cone of a lower face of $\operatorname{epi}(f)$ characterizes the subdifferential of $f$ at the interior of the face projected back onto coordinate space.
\hfill$\square$

label: lemma:dual_inclusion
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lemma:dual_inclusion}
Let $f : \mathbb{R}^{n} \rightarrow \mathbb{R} \cup \{\infty\}$ be convex piecewise linear. Let $\mathbf{F}, \mathbf{H} \in \mathcal{F}_f$ with corresponding $\partial f_{\mathbf{F}}, \partial f_{\mathbf{H}} \in \mathcal{F}_f^\star$, then $\mathbf{F}$ is a face of $\mathbf{H}$ if and only if $\partial f_\mathbf{H}$ is a face of $\partial f_{\mathbf{F}}$.
head: environment

label: prop:duality_of_complexes
title: Proposition
head: environment
name: Duality of complexes

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $g = f^\star$, then $g^\star = f$ by $f$ being closed and the Fenchel-Moreau theorem \cite[Corollary 13.38]{bauschke2011convex}. Therefore, $\mathcal{F}_f^\star = \mathcal{F}_{f^\star}$ is equivalent to $\mathcal{F}_{g^\star}^\star = \mathcal{F}_g$. Thus, we only need to prove $\mathcal{F}_{f^\star}^\star = \mathcal{F}_{f}$ for any convex piecewise linear function $f$.

A fundamental property of proper, closed, convex functions is the equivalence of the Fenchel-Young inequality \cite[Proposition 16.10]{bauschke2011convex}, i.e., if $\bm{x} \in \operatorname{dom}(f)$ and $\bm{y} \in \operatorname{dom}(f^\star)$, then
\begin{equation*}
    \bm{y} \in \partial f(\bm{x}) \,\text{\normalfont  if and only if }\bm{x} \in \partial f^\star(\bm{y}).
\end{equation*}

Let $\mathbf{F} \in \mathcal{F}_f$ and $\partial f_{\mathbf{F}} \in \mathcal{F}_f^\star$. We need to show that for all $\bm{y} \in \partial f_{\mathbf{F}}$, we have $\partial f^\star(\bm{y}) = \mathbf{F}$.

Let $\bm{y} \in \partial f_{\mathbf{F}}$ and $\bm{x} \in \operatorname{relint}(\mathbf{F})$, then $\bm{y} \in \partial f_{\mathbf{F}} = \partial f(\bm{x})$, thus $\bm{x} \in \partial f^\star(\bm{y})$, hence $\operatorname{relint}(\mathbf{F}) \subseteq \partial f^\star(\bm{y})$. Because the subdifferential is a closed set we get $\mathbf{F} \subseteq \partial f^\star(\bm{y})$.

Let $\bm{x} \in \mathbf{F}$ but $\bm{x} \not\in \partial f^\star(\bm{y})$. Then $\bm{y} \not\in \partial f(\bm{x})$. But by assumption $\bm{y} \in \partial f_{\mathbf{F}} \subseteq \partial f(\bm{x})$, which is a contradiction. 
\hfill$\square$
head: environment

label: prop:acyclic_vertex
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:acyclic_vertex}
    The vertices of the polytope $\mathbf{P}_{\text{TV}_G}$ are the vectors $\bm{z}_{\bm{u}} = \sum_{\{v_i, v_j\} \in \mathbf{E}} u_{i,j}\bm{d}_{i,j}$ with $\bm{u} \in \{-1,1\}^{\#\mathbf{E}}$ such that the associated directed graph is acyclic.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\bm{z}_{\bm{u}}$ such that the associated directed graph is cyclic. Because $\bm{z}_{\bm{u}} \in \mathbf{P}_{\text{TV}_G}$, there must exists $\bm{x}$ such that $\bm{z}_{\bm{u}} \in \partial \text{TV}_G (\bm{x})$, more specifically, the values in $\bm{x}$ must strictly increase over any directed link in the directed graph. Because the directed graph is cyclic, this results in a contradiction, hence the directed graph associated to $\bm{z}_{\bm{u}}$ is acyclic.

    Let $\bm{z}_{\bm{u}}$ such that the associated directed graph is acyclic. Construct $\bm{x} \in \mathbb{R}^{\#\mathbf{V}}$ inductively as follows. For each node $i$ with no in-going links, let $x_i = 0$. For all other nodes $j$, let $x_j$ be the one larger than the maximum over the $x_i$ from incoming nodes. By construction, $\text{TV}_G$ is differentiable at $\bm{x}$ with gradient $\bm{z}_{\bm{u}}$, hence $\bm{z}_{\bm{u}}$ is a vertex of the polytope $\mathbf{P}_{\text{TV}_G}$.
\hfill$\square$
head: environment

title: Corollary
body_md: An undirected graph $G$ is a tree, i.e., the graph does not have cycles, if and only if, the vertices of $\mathbf{P}_{\text{TV}_G}$ are all the vectors of the form $\sum_{\{v_i, v_j\} \in \mathbf{E}}u_{i,j}\bm{d}_{i,j}$ with $\bm{u} \in \{-1,1\}^{\#\mathbf{E}}$.
head: environment

label: prop:acyclic_vertex_NN
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:acyclic_vertex_NN}
    The vertices of $\mathbf{P}_{\text{TV}_G} - \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}^{\#\mathbf{V}}$ and $\mathbf{P}_{\text{TV}_G}$ are the same.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
If $\bm{v}$ be a vertex of $\mathbf{P}_{\text{TV}_G}$ that is not a vertex of $\mathbf{P}_{\text{TV}_G} - \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}^{\#\mathbf{V}}$, then $\bm{v}$ can be written as a convex combination of the other vertices of $\mathbf{P}_{\text{TV}_G}$ plus a non-zero vector $\bm{p}$ from the cone $-\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}^{\#\mathbf{V}}$. However, every vector $\bm{x} \in \mathbf{P}_{\text{TV}_G}$ satisfies $\bm{1}^T\bm{x} = 0$, but $\bm{1}^T\bm{v} = \bm{1}^T\bm{p} < 0$, a contradiction. Thus every vertex of $\mathbf{P}_{\text{TV}_G}$ is a vertex of $\mathbf{P}_{\text{TV}_G} - \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}^{\#\mathbf{V}}$. 
    
    For the converse, note that  vertices of the Minkowski sum of a polytope and a polyhedral cone are all vertices of the polytope.
\hfill$\square$
head: environment

label: def:level_set_complex
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:level_set_complex}
Let $f: \mathbb{R}^{n} \rightarrow \mathbb{R} \cup \{\infty\}$ be convex piecewise linear. For every $c \in \mathbb{R}$, define the level set $\mathcal{L}_f(c)$ as the polyhedral complex corresponding to the level set $\{\bm{x}\in \mathbb{R}^n\,|\, f(\bm{x}) = c\}$.
head: environment
name: level set complex

label: lem:levelsets_subsets
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:levelsets_subsets}
Let $f: \mathbb{R}^{n} \rightarrow \mathbb{R} \cup \{\infty\}$ be convex piecewise linear. If $\mathbf{L} \in \mathcal{L}_f(c)$ for some $c\in\mathbb{R}$ and $\bm{x} \in \operatorname{relint}(\mathbf{L})$ and $\bm{x} \in \mathbf{F} \in \mathcal{F}$, then $\mathbf{L} \subseteq \mathbf{F}$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Follows from the fact that the level set complex is part of the boundary of a polyhedral sublevel set of the epigraph.
\hfill$\square$

label: lem:codimension
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:codimension}
Let $f: \mathbb{R}^{n} \rightarrow \mathbb{R} \cup \{\infty\}$ be convex piecewise linear. Let $\partial f_{\mathbf{F}} \in \mathcal{F}_f^\star$. If $\operatorname{codim}(\partial f_{\mathbf{F}}) - \operatorname{rank}(A) = k > 0$ then $\dim(\operatorname{Null}(A) \cap \partial f_\mathbf{F}^\bot) = k$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We have $\operatorname{codim}(\partial f_{\mathbf{F}}) - \operatorname{rank}(A) = k$ if and only if $\dim(\partial f_{\mathbf{F}}^\bot) + \dim(\operatorname{Null}(A)) = n + k$.
Thus, because $n + k > n$, we get $\partial f_{\mathbf{F}}^\bot$ and $\operatorname{Null}(A)$ have a space of dimension $k$ in common.
\hfill$\square$
head: environment

label: prop:finding_two_solutions
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:finding_two_solutions}
Let $f: \mathbb{R}^{n} \rightarrow \mathbb{R} \cup \{\infty\}$ be convex piecewise linear, $A \in \mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$ and $\bm{x} \in \mathbf{F} \in \mathcal{F}_f$ with $\operatorname{codim}(\partial f_{\mathbf{F}}) - \operatorname{rank}(A) = k > 0 $. Then there exists $\mathbf{L} \in \mathcal{L}_f(f(\bm{x}))$ and a polyhedral set $\mathbf{S} \subseteq \mathbf{L} \subseteq \mathbf{F}$ for which $\bm{x} \in \mathbf{S}$, $\dim(\mathbf{S}) = k$ and $\mathbf{S} - \mathbf{S} \subseteq \operatorname{Null}(A)$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\mathbf{L} \in \mathcal{L}_f(f(\bm{x}))$ such that $\bm{x} \in \operatorname{relint}(\mathbf{L})$. If $\operatorname{codim}(\partial f_{\mathbf{F}}) - \operatorname{rank}(A) = k > 0 $, then by Lemma \ref{lem:codimension} and \ref{lem:subdifferential_orthogonal_level_set}, the set $\mathbf{S} = \left[\bm{x} + \operatorname{Null}(A) \cap \partial f_\mathbf{F}^\bot \right] \cap \mathbf{L}$ suffices.
\hfill$\square$
head: environment

label: prop:two_solutions_large_codimension
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\partial f_{\mathbf{F}} \in \mathcal{F}_f^\star$ be the smallest face of $\partial f(\bm{x}) \cap \partial f(\bm{y})$ such that $\operatorname{row}(A) \cap \partial f_{\mathbf{F}} \neq \emptyset$. Then by Lemma \ref{lemma:dual_inclusion}, $\bm{x},\bm{y}\in \mathbf{F}$. If $\operatorname{codim}(\partial f_{\mathbf{F}}) > \operatorname{rank}(A)$, we are done. So assume that $\operatorname{codim}(\partial f_{\mathbf{F}}) \leq \operatorname{rank}(A)$, or equivalently $\dim(\mathbf{F}) \leq \operatorname{rank}(A)$, then,
\begin{equation*}
    \dim(A(\mathbf{F}-\mathbf{F})) < \dim(\mathbf{F}-\mathbf{F}) = \dim(\mathbf{F}) \leq \operatorname{rank}(A).
\end{equation*}
Thus, the strict inclusion $A(\mathbf{F}-\mathbf{F}) \subset \operatorname{col}(A)$, equivalently $\operatorname{Null}(A^T) \subset (A(\mathbf{F}-\mathbf{F}))^\bot$ holds. Therefore, there exists $\bm{d} \in \mathbb{R}^m$ such that $A^T\bm{d} \neq \bm{0}$ and $(\mathbf{F}-\mathbf{F})^TA^T\bm{d} = \{\bm{0}\}$, hence $\bm{0} \neq A^T\bm{d} \in \partial f_{\mathbf{F}}^\bot$.

By assumption, there also exists $\bm{z} \in \mathbb{R}^m$ such that $A^T\bm{z} \in \partial f_{\mathbf{F}}$.
Now consider the line $A^T\bm{z} + tA^T\bm{d}$ for $t\in \mathbb{R}^n$. By construction, this line is contained in $\operatorname{row}(A) \cap \partial f_{\mathbf{F}}$. However, by the assumption that $\dim(\operatorname{dom}(f)) = n$, $\partial f_{\mathbf{F}}$ cannot contain a line, hence $\operatorname{row}(A)$ must intersect a face of $\partial f_{\mathbf{F}}$, which is a contradiction.
\hfill$\square$
head: environment

label: lem:equal_fit
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Assume that $\bm{x} \neq \bm{y}$ and $A\bm{x}\neq A\bm{y}$. By strict convexity of $D(\cdot, \bm{b})$ we have that for $\bm{z} = \frac{1}{2}(\bm{x} + \bm{y})$,
\begin{equation*}
    D(\bm{z}, \bm{b}) + f(\bm{z}) < \frac{1}{2}\left[D(A\bm{x}, \bm{b}) + f(\bm{x}) + D(A\bm{y}, \bm{b}) + f(\bm{y})\right] = \min_{\bm{v}\in\mathbb{R}^n}\left\{D(A\bm{v}, \bm{b}) + f(\bm{v}) \right\}.
\end{equation*}
This contradicts $\bm{x}, \bm{y} \in \mathbf{S}^D_{A, f}(\bm{b})$.

Because $\bm{x}, \bm{y} \in \mathbf{S}^D_{A, f}(\bm{b})$ and $A\bm{x} = A\bm{y}$, we get $f(\bm{x}) = f(\bm{y})$.
\hfill$\square$
head: environment

label: thm:nec_uniqueness
title: Theorem
body_md:
(Necessary condition for uniqueness)\label{thm:nec_uniqueness}
Let $D:\mathbb{R}^m\times\mathbb{R}^m \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ be arbitrary.
If there exist $\bm{x} \in \mathbf{S}_{A, f}^{D}(\bm{b})$ for some $\bm{b} \in \mathbb{R}^m$ and let $\mathbf{F} \in \mathcal{F}_f$ containing $\bm{x}$ such that $\operatorname{codim}(\partial f_{\mathbf{F}}) - \operatorname{rank}(A) = k > 0$, then $\dim(\mathbf{S}_{A, f}^{D}(\bm{b})) \geq k$.

Thus, if $\#[\mathbf{F} \cap \mathbf{S}_{A, f}^{D}(\bm{b})] \leq 1$ for all $\bm{b} \in \mathbb{R}^m$ and $\mathbf{F} \in \mathcal{F}_f$, then $\#[\mathbf{F} \cap \mathbf{S}_{A, f}^{D}(\bm{b})] = 1$ must imply $\operatorname{codim}(\partial f_{\mathbf{F}}) \leq \operatorname{rank}(A).$
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Follows directly from Proposition \ref{prop:finding_two_solutions}.
\hfill$\square$
head: environment

label: thm:suf_uniqueness
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:suf_uniqueness}
Let $D: \mathbb{R}^m\times\mathbb{R}^m \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ be strictly convex and differentiable in its first argument and $\dim(\operatorname{dom}(f)) = n$. If $\#\mathbf{S}_{A, f}^{D}(\bm{b}) > 1$ for some $\bm{b} \in \mathbb{R}^m$, then there exists $\mathbf{F} \in \mathcal{F}_f$ such that $\operatorname{row}(A) \cap \partial f_{\mathbf{F}}$ and $\operatorname{codim}(\partial f_{\mathbf{F}}) > \operatorname{rank}(A)$.
head: environment
name: sufficient condition for uniqueness

title: Proof
head: environment

label: cor:nec_suf_un
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:nec_suf_un}
Let $D : \mathbb{R}^m \times \mathbb{R}^m \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ be a smooth data fidelity function, $A\in \mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$ be a linear operator and $f:\mathbb{R}^n \rightarrow \mathbb{R} \cup \{\infty\}$ be a convex piecewise linear function. If $\dim(\operatorname{dom}(f)) = n$, then $\#\mathbf{S}_{A,f}^D(\bm{b}) = 1$ for all $\bm{b}\in\mathbb{R}^m$ if and only if $\operatorname{row}(A) \cap \partial f_{\mathbf{F}} \neq \emptyset$ implies $\operatorname{codim}(\partial f_{\mathbf{F}}) \leq \operatorname{rank}(A)$. That is, every accessible set $\mathbf{F}$ must satisfy $\operatorname{codim}(\partial f_{\mathbf{F}}) \leq \operatorname{rank}(A)$.
head: environment
name: Necessary and sufficient conditions for uniqueness

label: lem:uniqueness_implies_piecewise_linear
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:uniqueness_implies_piecewise_linear}
Let $D : \mathbb{R}^m \times \mathbb{R}^m \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ be $D(\bm{x}, \bm{y}) = \frac12\|\bm{x} - \bm{y}\|^2_{\Sigma}$, $A \in \mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$ be a linear operator and $f:\mathbb{R}^n \rightarrow \mathbb{R} \cup \{\infty\}$ be a convex piecewise linear function. If $\mathbf{S}^D_{A, f}$ is single-valued, then for all $\mathbf{F} \in \mathcal{F}_f$, the inverse image $[S^D_{A,f}]^{-1}(\mathbf{F})$ is closed and convex and the restricted solution map $S^D_{A, f}\big|_{[S^D_{A,f}]^{-1}(\mathbf{F})}$ is affine.
head: environment
name: uniqueness implies piecewise linear

title: Proof
head: environment

label: thm:uniqueness_implies_continuity
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:uniqueness_implies_continuity}
Let $D : \mathbb{R}^m \times \mathbb{R}^m \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ be $D(\bm{x}, \bm{y}) = \|\bm{x} - \bm{y}\|^2_{\Sigma}$, $A \in \mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$ be a linear operator and $f:\mathbb{R}^n \rightarrow \mathbb{R} \cup \{\infty\}$ be a convex piecewise linear function. If $\mathbf{S}_{A, f}$ is single-valued, then $S_{A,f}$ is continuous.
head: environment
name: uniqueness implies continuity

title: Proof
body_md:
By Corollary \ref{cor:range_solution_set}, there exists a polyhedral subcomplex $\mathcal{E} \subseteq \mathcal{F}_f$ such that $\operatorname{range}(S_{A, f}) = \bigcup_{\mathbf{F}\in \mathcal{E}}\mathbf{F}$. Due to Lemma \ref{lem:uniqueness_implies_piecewise_linear}, the domain of $S_{A,f}$ can be covered by closed sets, i.e., $\operatorname{dom}(S_{A, f}) = \mathbb{R}^m = \bigcup_{\mathbf{F}\in \mathcal{E}}[S^D_{A,f}]^{-1}(\mathbf{F})$. The solution map $S_{A, f}$ restricted to each closed covering element $[S^D_{A,f}]^{-1}(\mathbf{F})$ is affine, hence continuous. Because the function coincided on the intersection of the covering elements, the continuity of $S_{A,f}$ follows from the pasting lemma \cite[Theorem 18.3]{Munkres2014topology}.
\hfill$\square$
head: environment

label: thm:almost_surely_wellposed
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:almost_surely_wellposed}
    Let $f : \mathbb{R}^n \rightarrow \cup \{\infty\}$ be a convex piecewise linear function with $\dim(\operatorname{dom}(f)) = n$ and $p$ be the dimension of the smallest subdifferential $\partial f_{\mathbf{F}} \in \mathcal{F}_f^{\star}$ that contains the zero vector. If $A \in \mathbb{R}^{m \times n}$ with $m \geq p$ is a continuously distributed random matrix, then the linear least squares problem for $A$ regularized by $f$ is almost surely well-posed.

label: thm:well-posedness_conp-hard
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:well-posedness_conp-hard}
Let $f_n(\bm{x})$ be either $\gamma \|\bm{x}\|_1$, $\gamma \|D_n\bm{x}\|_1$ or $\gamma \|D_n\bm{x}\|_1 + \chi_{\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}^n}$ with finite difference matrix $D_{n} \in \mathbb{R}^{(n-1)\times n}$ and $\gamma > 0$. Then, verifying well-posedness of $A\in \mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$ with respect to $f_n(\bm{x})$ is co-NP-hard.
head: environment
